memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Patient reports retrosternal burning after meals, occasional regurgitation, and nighttime cough. On examination: mild epigastric tenderness, no hepatomegaly. Smoking status: never. Prescribed pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, and antacid gel SOS. Advised lifestyle modifications: elevate head of bed, avoid spicy/fatty meals, and weight review.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Since starting pantoprazole, my heartburn has improved markedly; I only need antacid gel once or twice a week. No nighttime symptoms.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, stable. Patient reports occasional mild heartburn after large meals, relieved by antacid gel. No alarm symptoms. Examination: soft abdomen, no tenderness. Continued current PPI dose. Advised to maintain lifestyle measures and review in 3 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past month, heartburn has returned, especially after dinner, and I feel a sour taste in the mouth. Antacid gel helps but I need it almost daily.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, symptomatic despite standard PPI. Patient reports worsening heartburn and regurgitation, nocturnal symptoms affecting sleep. No dysphagia, weight loss, or anemia. Examination: mild epigastric tenderness. Decided to pursue upper GI endoscopy to exclude erosive esophagitis or Barrett’s changes.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Upper GI endoscopy: Los Angeles grade A erosive esophagitis in distal 2 cm; no Barrett’s epithelium. Biopsy negative for H. pylori and dysplasia.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, improved on twice‑daily pantoprazole. Patient reports only occasional mild heartburn after heavy meals, no nocturnal symptoms. Examination: benign abdomen. Plan to step down therapy after confirming sustained control.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been taking pantoprazole twice daily as prescribed. My symptoms are mostly gone; I only feel slight discomfort after very large meals, which resolves with an antacid.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, well controlled. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Patient on pantoprazole 40 mg BD wishes to reduce medication due to long‑term use. Technique checked: correct for inhaler (not used). Decision: taper pantoprazole to 20 mg OD and monitor for symptom recurrence.
